grade.first_issue: In Step 3, the assertion that for every n one can choose a nonnegative orbit index m with |u_n-v_m|≤c_2 is false when u_n lies well below z_2. It should say “for all sufficiently large n.” This is a minor quantifier overstatement, not a Rule C load-bearing falsehood, because only the large-n sequence is used and the corrected claim follows immediately by rounding.
grade.summary: The submitted solution correctly obtains the iterate identity, proves g≥0, compares positive-defect orbits to show all positive values of g coincide, excludes coexistence of defects 0 and c, and verifies every translation f(x)=x+c. Apart from the harmless finite-prefix quantifier error in the orbit comparison, the proof is coherent and complete.
strengths: Correctly derives f(f(y))=2f(y)-y and hence invariance of g along forward orbits.
Uses positivity of all iterates to establish g(x)≥0.
The bounded-distance orbit comparison correctly forces any two positive values of g to be equal.
The neighborhood-propagation argument rules out simultaneous zero and positive defect values.
The converse is verified correctly using RMS–AM and AM–GM.

errors.description: The bounded-distance choice of m is guaranteed only once u_n is at least z_2, not for every n as stated. Restricting to sufficiently large n repairs the argument without changing its limit conclusion.
